claims.claim: Since 2023 a non-Muslim foreigner's estate follows the civil personal status law (or home-country law, if chosen) rather than Sharia

sources.name: Withers: estate planning for non-Muslims and residents in the UAE
sources.says: Dated 7 October 2024. Under "Federal Decree-Law No. (41) of 2022 on Civil Personal Status", with changes for non-Muslims "introduced in 2023", a non-Muslim's estate without a will is "distributed without a distinction between genders", unlike Sharia; non-Muslim foreigners residing in the UAE may "decide to follow the laws of their home country". The DIFC Wills Service Centre "facilitates the registration of English language wills by non-Muslims".

claims.note: A 2024 law-firm page, older than the source order's 2025–26 for secondary pages; the Ministry of Justice's copy of Federal Decree-Law 41 of 2022 (elaws.moj.gov.ae) refused the connection and the u.ae wills page tried was a 404.

claims.claim: The $15M US exemption (2026) is the only relief

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
sources.says: "Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000", up from $13,990,000 for 2025; the release (October 9, 2025) cites Revenue Procedure 2025-32 and is marked as an archival document.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.

claims.claim: Health insurance is compulsory for Dubai residents

sources.name: Dubai Legal Portal: Law No. (11) of 2013 regulating health insurance in the Emirate of Dubai
sources.says: Article 7(a): "The entities determined in Article (9) of this Law must enrol UAE Nationals, Residents and Visitors in Health Insurance"; Article 9(a): employers enrol employees and "a Sponsor will be responsible for enroling the persons he sponsors who do not have an Employer"; cover cannot be less than the Basic Coverage.

sources.name: The National: are high insurance costs pricing retirees out of the UAE?
sources.says: Dated July 11, 2024. "There are no specific packages for retired people." Basic annual plans "can start at about Dh5,000" but use lower-cost hospitals; a 67-year-old retiree went from about Dh30,000 to over Dh90,000 at renewal after a knee operation and now pays "just over Dh25,000" on a basic policy. "In Dubai, companies can load up to 100 per cent of the current premium per condition." Health insurance is mandatory in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
